title: Mechanism Graph
description: DISCOVER-stage deep-ideation artifact. Output of the mechanism-graph-builder worker. The EXPLICIT internal causal/dependency graph of the TARGET problem itself — distinct from mechanism_mapping (which is a CROSS-domain analogy between a source domain and this problem). This is where 'depth' becomes a measurable object instead of a longer paragraph: the problem is decomposed into mechanism / variable / mediator / outcome nodes and the directed causal edges between them, plus the points where one could intervene and the known failure modes. Descriptive ONLY — it asserts no novelty, feasibility, ranking, or selection (no verdict / chosen / bet field; additionalProperties:false everywhere). Anti-slop: every node and every edge carries a non-empty evidence_ref; every present string is non-blank (pattern \S). Graph metrics (depth, branch count, unclosed-chain count) are computed downstream by idea_quality_eval, never hand-set here. Domain-general: node labels may use domain-surface phrasing, but the graph STRUCTURE is the unit of depth. Cross-field integrity (every edge from_node/to_node names a real node_id) is enforced by the producing recipe, mirroring the tournament-pair integrity check.

graph_id.description: Short unique identifier for this graph, e.g. MG-001. Non-blank.

problem_ref.description: The problem_abstraction.problem_id this graph decomposes (e.g. PA-001). Real-ref guard: must contain a digit, so a flag-word cannot be smuggled through this field.

nodes.description: The mechanism nodes of the problem. At least 2 (a graph needs >=2 nodes to carry an edge). Each node is a mechanism, variable, mediator, intervention point, or outcome.

node_id.description: Identifier unique within this graph, e.g. N1. Referenced by edges. Non-blank.

label.description: What this node is, e.g. 'frozen-encoder feature drift'. Non-blank.

kind.description: The role of this node in the causal graph.

evidence_ref.description: Anti-slop: at least one non-blank pointer (a real [[slug]], gap_id, or claim_id) grounding that this mechanism is real, not invented.

edges.description: Directed relations between nodes — the causal/dependency structure. At least 1 (a graph with zero edges is a node list, not a mechanism graph). Depth = the longest from->to chain (computed downstream).

edge_id.description: Identifier unique within this graph, e.g. E1. Non-blank.

from_node.description: node_id this edge starts at (must name a real node — the recipe enforces it). Non-blank.

to_node.description: node_id this edge points to (must name a real node — the recipe enforces it). Non-blank.

evidence_ref.description: Anti-slop: at least one non-blank pointer grounding that this relation is real, not invented.

rationale.description: Optional one-line justification of why the relation holds.

intervention_points.description: Where one could ACT to change the outcome (the levers). MAY be empty. Each names a node_id and why it is actionable.

node_ref.description: node_id of an intervention_point/mechanism node one could act on. Non-blank.

rationale.description: Why acting here would change the outcome. Non-blank.

failure_modes.description: How this mechanism is known to break / be hard (mechanism-level phrasing preferred). MAY be empty. Each present item is a non-blank string.

notes.description: Optional clarifying notes (e.g. north-star drift, uncertainty in a relation).
